The Merge activates 4399 and 3675 on the execution layer https://i.redd.it/3f3uic4ttlr71.jpg I belive that is where it came from Etherscan shows 0x000....000 as the fee receipient for some, but not all empty blocks: is this caused by a specific client combo issue? Ah, looks weird but ok our lodestar nodes (70-80k range) haven't set any fee recipient, so default is 0x0s, will update to some value On etherscan difficulty is still shown as 0 though rather than prevrandao value. it is 0 in the block header [explainer graph incoming] https://blog.ethereum.org/2021/11/29/how-the-merge-impacts-app-layer/ it goes into mixHash in the header The `0x44` opcode, pre-merge, returns `difficulty`, but post-merge it points to a different value, `prevRandao`, which is stored in the `mixHash` field of the EL block headers. We did not want to store `prevRandao` in `difficulty` to not cause weird issues in clients if the difficulty in headers suddenly jumps a ton. Similarly, we didn't want to change the EL block header format, which would break tooling. That makes sense. Thanks for explaining! What happens to contract that expects difficulty from 0x44 opcode as it was before the merge? They still get a pseudorandom value, just a different one 🙂 Difficulty is difficulty, not a pseudorandom number, the difficulty is predictable. Before the merge it’s stable difficulty, but once merge happens it goes to 2^256. What if the application relies on the difficulty change? Well, no matter what at the Merge the difficulty does change In practice we see a lot of apps use this as (bad) pseudo randomness So the goal is to not brick all of those by always returning 0 If your app relies on a difficulty changing within a normal POW bound, then there is no way to keep it working post merge: either you get 0 or PREVRANDAO I think seeing a difficulty increase by 7493613713105269057212779901749642368683842602632163689206353x in a single block doesn't sound right. Same with going to 0, though? Correct. Both options are similarly outrageous. So basically it was a choice what applications to bork, and what to leave functional? Do you know how applications used this opcode? Impossible to review every single EVM application out there in the world. no, not at all. this has been discussed for a while, and those who participated indicated that difficulty was used as a source of entropy so now that entropy has

excerpts.author: timbeiko
excerpts.content: The `0x44` opcode, pre-merge, returns `difficulty`, but post-merge it points to a different value, `prevRandao`, which is stored in the `mixHash` field of the EL block headers. We did not want to store `prevRandao` in `difficulty` to not cause weird issues in clients if the difficulty in headers suddenly jumps a ton. Similarly, we didn't want to change the EL block header format, which would break tooling.
